name: Xeroderma Pigmentosum

ethnicAssociations: Higher prevalence in Japan, North Africa, Middle East

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Molecular Diagnostic Criteria for Xeroderma Pigmentosum

criteria.description: Extreme sensitivity to ultraviolet (UV) light with severe sunburn reactions
Development of multiple early-onset skin cancers including basal cell carcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma, and melanoma
Deficient nucleotide excision repair demonstrated by cellular assays or genetic testing identifying pathogenic variants in XP genes
Presence of photophobia, keratitis, or conjunctival abnormalities
Progressive neurological abnormalities such as sensorineural hearing loss or cognitive decline

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of extreme UV sensitivity with early-onset skin cancers plus confirmation of DNA repair defect by molecular or cellular testing
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is confirmatory; clinical diagnosis may be suspected based on history and skin findings.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Extreme photosensitivity with severe sunburn reactions

searchTerms: frequent skin tumors at young age

pathognomonic.symptomName: Poikiloderma with mottled pigmentation and skin atrophy
searchTerms: skin with mixed pigmentation and atrophy
red eyes with visible small blood vessels
eye redness and tiny dilated vessels

common.symptomName: Freckling in sun-exposed areas before age 2
searchTerms: freckles on sun skin before age 2
freckling in sun areas very young

laboratory: Cellular hypersensitivity to UV radiation in fibroblast cultures
Reduced nucleotide excision repair capacity assays
imaging: MRI brain may show cerebral atrophy in patients with neurological involvement
genetic: Pathogenic variants in XP genes (e.g., XPA, XPB, XPC, XPD, XPE, XPF, XPG)
other: Skin biopsy showing solar elastosis and atypical keratinocytes
Early onset skin cancers confirmed by histopathology

distinguishingFeatures: Growth failure and developmental delay prominent
No extreme UV sensitivity or early skin cancers
Characteristic facial features and progressive neurological degeneration
Photosensitivity without high skin cancer risk

redFlags: Severe sunburn after minimal UV exposure in infancy
Progressive neurological decline in a child with photosensitivity
